description: Trigger, routing, and output-quality cases for the workload health summary skill. Positive cases select overview or drill-down, keep output read-only, surface dominant patterns, and hand off root-cause diagnosis instead of guessing.

evals.prompt: In cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, list workloads that failed between 2026-05-31T10:42:00Z and 2026-05-31T10:52:00Z and tell me if this looks like a node issue.
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, applies phase=Failed and both bounds of the explicit 10-minute window with includeDetails=true, and stays within the 50-workload correlation budget. It includes workload_id, project, department, status_changed_at, node, kind, priority, and preemptibility for every failed row. It may flag node-a-04 as LIKELY_NODE_ISSUE only after status returns node-specific phase evidence, pod placement and timing are complete, and independent infrastructure evidence reports node-a-04 NotReady. Pool size alone is not treated as scheduling eligibility. It does not claim root cause.
expected_behavior: requires cluster_id and a failed-workload overview filter
uses includeDetails=true on the complete scoped list_workloads result
applies phaseUpdatedAfter and an upper-bound phaseUpdatedAt filter
uses status for phase time, phaseMessage, phaseReason, and ownership plus pods for placement
uses independent node health rather than pool size alone before a likely node-issue label
includes owner attribution
keeps workload_id in every row
does not diagnose root cause

evals.prompt: Which workloads are on node-a-04 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001?
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, calls get_node_pods with limit=200 and follows hasMore/nextOffset within the 1,000-pod budget, deduplicates workload IDs, and lists workloads on node-a-04 with workload_id, phase, kind, project, and department. It does not call metrics unless the user asks for a metric-based sort or filter.
expected_behavior: uses paginated get_node_pods with nodeName, clusterUuid, limit, and offset
reports truncation instead of claiming completeness if the paging budget is exceeded
includes workload_id and owner
uses bounded status enrichment for each unique workload because get_node_pods omits phase and ownership
does not call metrics without a metric filter or ranking
does not infer cause for failed workloads on the node

evals.prompt: Show workloads idle for more than 6 hours in project ml-team on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, calls list_workloads with project=ml-team, gpuIdleOnly=true, and includeDetails=true, then requests metrics only for those candidates because the request includes gpu_idle_for>6h. It states the threshold and reports idle-eval-7 as DEGRADED or an idle candidate only if returned metric timing supports it, without diagnosing why it is idle.
expected_behavior: starts with project-scoped list_workloads using gpuIdleOnly=true and includeDetails=true
applies metrics after cheap filters
does not use workload age or phase duration as GPU idle duration
reports the idle threshold
keeps workload_id in every row
does not invent an idle root cause

evals.prompt: What failed in the Research department between 2026-05-31T10:22:00Z and 2026-05-31T10:52:00Z on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001?
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, filters by department=Research plus phase=Failed and both bounds of the explicit 30-minute window with includeDetails=true, leads with a dominant pattern if at least 70% share a field, and includes workload_id and owner. A node-issue label requires complete placement and reliable timing, no shared workload-level explanation, and either actual scheduling-eligibility evidence or independent node evidence; co-location or pool size alone is reported only as CORRELATED_FAILURES.
expected_behavior: uses list_workloads with a departmentName comparison and includeDetails=true
applies both timestamp bounds
surfaces dominant pattern at 70 percent concentration
includes workload_id
does not do root-cause analysis

evals.prompt: Any failed inference workloads in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001?
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, filters failed inference workloads, includes workload_id and owner, marks SLA-bearing inference rows as escalation candidates, and routes cause questions to the appropriate diagnostic skill.
expected_behavior: filters kind=Inference and phase=Failed
marks inference as SLA-bearing
includes owner attribution
does not infer cause

evals.prompt: Which unhealthy workloads are using image nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.05-py3 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001?
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, applies cheap health filters first, then checks submitted specs only for a bounded set of at most 10 candidates because the current MCP list schema cannot filter by image. It leads with a dominant image or phase pattern, keeps the output capped, and asks the user to narrow scope rather than performing unbounded spec calls.
expected_behavior: states that image requires bounded post-fetch spec checks
asks the user to narrow scope instead of inspecting more than 10 candidate specs
does not call get_workloads_summary before the row-producing query
caps output by default limit
groups before listing
uses status and pods only for matched failed rows because failed-overview node correlation is mandatory

evals.prompt: Show running workloads in ml-team sorted by restart count on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode and uses project and phase filters first. Because restart count is not exposed by the current Run:ai MCP pod schema, it uses optional read-only Kubernetes evidence or explicitly reports that restart sorting is unavailable; it never invents restart counts.
expected_behavior: uses cheap project and phase filters first
does not claim MCP exposes restart counts
uses read-only Kubernetes evidence when available or reports the field unavailable
avoids root-cause diagnosis

evals.prompt: List failed workloads in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, limit 2.
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in overview mode, applies phase=Failed with includeDetails=true, reads the complete scoped failed set before display capping, and performs correlation only when at most 50 candidates exist. It shows 2 rows, reports that output is capped, and offers to widen. If the set exceeds the correlation budget, it reports correlation incomplete and suppresses node-issue labels.
expected_behavior: applies the requested limit
mentions capped output
includes workload_id in each shown row
bounds correlation enrichment to at most 50 failed workloads
suppresses node-issue labels when evidence or budget is incomplete

evals.expected_output: The skill activates in drill-down mode, returns State, Spec, Pods, Metrics, and Policy/Notes in order, judges MCP-only pod health from returned pod phases, and does not invent desired/ready or restart counts. It computes a GPU-memory percentage only against the allocatedResources.gpuMemory value returned by spec and otherwise reports absolute bytes. It ends with Status: HEALTHY.
expected_behavior: calls get_workload_status
calls get_workload_spec
calls get_workload_pods
calls get_workload_metrics
calls get_workload_effective_policy when available
does not mark missing optional readiness as degraded
labels the allocated GPU-memory denominator when computing a percentage
ends with a one-line HEALTHY verdict

evals.prompt: Something seems off with workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000043 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001. What is its health?
evals.expected_output: The skill activates in drill-down mode, returns the five sections, flags low GPU use from metrics, does not invent a restart count, and ends with Status: DEGRADED rather than diagnosing the root cause.
expected_behavior: returns five ordered sections
does not claim a restart count without Kubernetes evidence
flags idle or low GPU use
does not route unless the user asks for cause
ends with DEGRADED

evals.prompt: Is training-job-42 healthy in project ml-team on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001?
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves training-job-42 by exact workload name and project using projectName.value=ml-team. If multiple exact candidates remain, it asks the user to choose by full workload_id and makes no drill-down calls. It selects the most recent candidate only when the user explicitly asks for the latest run.
expected_behavior: uses list_workloads with exact name and projectName for resolution
uses the project name rather than the workload name as projectName.value
filters exact workload name matches
uses project context
asks for clarification instead of choosing the newest match by default
returns drill-down only after the workload is unambiguous

evals.prompt: Is inference-prod-9 healthy right now in project finance-prod on cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001?
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the inference workload and summarizes only the throughput, latency, or NIM time-series values and labels actually returned. It does not invent percentiles, targets, request rates, or error rates, and routes latency root cause elsewhere if the user asks why it is slow.
expected_behavior: uses drill-down mode for one workload
includes inference-specific returned metrics when available
does not invent latency percentiles or targets
does not perform inference root-cause diagnosis

evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary must NOT activate; this is root-cause diagnosis for a known failed workload and should route to runai-diagnose-failed-workload.
expected_behavior: does not activate health summary
routes to failed-workload diagnosis
does not load or execute the destination workflow in the same turn
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Why was my workload preempted?
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary must NOT activate for preemption root-cause diagnosis; route to runai-diagnose-preempted-workload when available.
expected_behavior: does not activate health summary
routes preemption cause to the preempted-workload diagnostic
does not load or execute the destination workflow in the same turn
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Why is inference-prod-9 slow and missing its latency SLO?
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary must NOT perform inference latency root-cause diagnosis; route to runai-diagnose-inference-latency when available.
expected_behavior: does not use health summary for latency root cause
routes slow inference diagnosis to the inference-latency skill
does not load or execute the destination workflow in the same turn
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Which projects are starved for GPU quota and who is over-borrowing?
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary must NOT activate; this is quota fairness and should route to runai-audit-assigned-quota.
expected_behavior: does not activate health summary
routes to quota audit
does not load or execute the destination workflow in the same turn
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Show me every workload in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.
evals.expected_output: The skill must not dump the whole cluster without a useful health scope. It asks for a filter such as project, department, phase, node, age, image, kind, owner, or idle threshold and makes zero MCP calls. A limit alone would not provide scope.
expected_behavior: requires at least one overview filter
does not return an unbounded cluster-wide list
asks for scope
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Find all failed workloads from the last hour and delete them.
evals.expected_output: The health-summary skill must not query or delete workloads for this mutation request. It names the appropriate write-capable workflow, states that no action will be taken without explicit confirmation in that separate workflow, and makes zero MCP calls.
expected_behavior: routes mutation to a write-capable workflow
does not call mutating tools
requires confirmation before bulk action
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Training-job-42 looks okay to me; confirm whether it needs diagnosis.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the missing cluster_id and project or workload_id, then stops without calling MCP. It does not invent a problem or hand off to diagnosis.
expected_behavior: asks for missing cluster and project or workload_id before tool calls
makes zero MCP calls before scope is supplied
does not hand off for a healthy workload
does not invent a problem

evals.prompt: Workload idle-eval-7 in project ml-team looks degraded. Tell me what exactly caused it.
evals.expected_output: This is a root-cause request, so the health-summary skill names the most specific matching diagnostic workflow and stops without collecting a health snapshot. It makes zero MCP calls and does not invent a cause.
expected_behavior: recognizes root-cause intent before health collection
does not invent root cause
hands off to a runai-diagnose-* workflow when cause is requested
does not load or execute the destination workflow in the same turn
makes zero MCP calls

evals.expected_output: The skill should report PENDING as a health verdict when the user asks for state. If a direct startup failure is present and the user asks why, route to runai-diagnose-failed-workload.
expected_behavior: uses PENDING as a health verdict
distinguishes state from cause
routes direct startup failure causes to failed-workload diagnosis

evals.prompt: Why is this workload Pending because it cannot get resources?
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary should not perform Pending-workload root-cause diagnosis. It should route scheduling-only Pending diagnosis to the appropriate pending or scheduling workflow when available.
expected_behavior: does not classify scheduling-only Pending as failed
does not use failed-workload diagnosis unless direct pod-start failure exists
routes or asks for the pending-diagnosis workflow
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Give me a health snapshot for workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, but policy data is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: The skill should still return State, Spec, Pods, Metrics, and Policy/Notes. Policy/Notes should say policy data is unavailable instead of retrying broadly or failing the whole answer.
expected_behavior: keeps the five-section format
reports unavailable policy data
does not fail the whole drill-down
does not invent policy values

evals.prompt: Summarize workload health for workload 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000046 in cluster 20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001; metrics are empty.
evals.expected_output: The skill should report the missing metric in Metrics or Policy/Notes and avoid inferring idle time, memory pressure, latency, or error rate from state alone.
expected_behavior: reports missing metrics explicitly
does not fabricate utilization or latency
uses remaining state/spec/pod evidence

evals.prompt: Is the cluster healthy and is the scheduler stuck?
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary should not replace cluster-health analysis. It should route to runai-get-cluster-health-summary when available.
expected_behavior: does not activate for broad cluster health
routes to cluster-health summary
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Which teams are wasting GPU cycles across the whole cluster?
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary does not replace a utilization-efficiency overview. It names runai-get-utilization-overview and stops with zero MCP calls, even if that workflow is unavailable.
expected_behavior: does not use workload health summary for broad utilization waste
routes to utilization overview
makes zero MCP calls

evals.expected_output: This is a simple state question. The skill calls get_workload_status first and, when status shows completion without failure, answers from that response and stops. It does not fetch spec, pods, metrics, policy, or Kubernetes evidence and does not route to diagnosis.
expected_behavior: reports successful state
stops after get_workload_status when status is conclusive
does not fetch unrelated drill-down evidence
does not invent failure

evals.prompt: Compare the current healthy run with yesterday's run.
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary does not perform run-to-run comparison. It names the comparison workflow and stops with zero MCP calls, even if that workflow is unavailable.
expected_behavior: does not use health summary as a run-comparison workflow
does not fabricate historical data
names the comparison workflow
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Restart every degraded workload in ml-team.
evals.expected_output: The skill must not query or restart workloads for this mutation request. It names the appropriate write-capable workflow, requires explicit confirmation there, and makes zero MCP calls.
expected_behavior: does not call write tools
requires confirmation before any bulk action
routes to a write-capable workflow
makes zero MCP calls

evals.prompt: Summarize this pull request.
evals.expected_output: runai-get-workload-health-summary must NOT activate; the request is unrelated to Run:ai workload health.
expected_behavior: does not activate health summary
makes zero MCP calls
